question: A and B together can complete a job in 8 days. If A alone can do it in 16 days, how many days will B alone take?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let **Total Work** be the **LCM** of 8 and 16 = **16 units**.

Efficiency of **(A + B)** = 16 ÷ 8 = **2 units/day**.

Efficiency of **A** = 16 ÷ 16 = **1 unit/day**.

Efficiency of **B** = 2 − 1 = **1 unit/day**.

Time taken by **B** = 16 ÷ 1 = **16 days**.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Time taken by **(A + B)** = 8 days | Time taken by **A** = 16 days.

**Formula Used:** Total Work = Efficiency × Time | Efficiency of B = Efficiency of (A+B) − Efficiency of A.

⇒ Efficiency of **B** = Efficiency of **(A + B)** − Efficiency of **A**

⇒ Efficiency of **B** = 2 − 1 = **1 unit/day**

⇒ Time taken by **B** = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of **B**

⇒ Time taken by **B** = 16 ÷ 1 = **16 days**

**∴ The correct answer is 16 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work and Efficiency Relation

**Efficiency** is inversely proportional to **Time** taken when **Work** is constant. If time ratio is x : y, efficiency ratio is y : x.

Total Work Formula

**Total Work** = **Efficiency** × **Time**. For multiple people, total efficiency is the sum of their individual efficiencies.

Pipes and Cisterns

This logic applies to **Pipes and Cisterns**, where an outlet pipe has **negative efficiency** (work done in removing water).</p
